subject: Post-demo checklist — concurrency targets, k6 scripts, and allowlist window
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo checklist — concurrency targets, k6 scripts, and allowlist window

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned for the customer-led run: 

Summary from call:
- Target SLOs: <100ms median for single-turn text generation, 95th <350ms for 1k-token streaming sessions.
- Throughput needs: sustained 120 requests/sec for sync generation profile; streaming clients expect 300 concurrent streams with average 40 tokens/sec.
- Test types: ramp + soak for sync endpoints (k6), streaming probe (custom Locust/k6 hybrid).

Proposed handoff items from Streamline AI (what we need from you):
1) k6 scenario bundle (scripts + env file) for the sync profile.
2) Specification of the streaming client behavior (avg token cadence, connection lifetime).
3) IP allowlist for Redwood test ingress or let us know if you’ll run clients from your infra.
4) Preferred 3-hour test window (we recommend a weekday evening UTC-friendly slot).

We can provide a pre-provisioned test account and temporary API key, plus a simple traffic matrix and expected observability spans. I’ve attached a short SLO summary and will loop Marissa/Ben for the test ops side. 

Attachments: slo-targets-summary.pdf (summary), sample test matrix (in Drive link)

Next steps (can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?):
- Send k6 bundle + anything we should know about authentication or long-poll behavior
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to originate traffic (we’ll provide an IP list) or if you run from your side
- Preferred window (we suggested Thu 9/9 22:00–01:00 UTC as an option)

Thanks — I’ll prepare the runbook once I have the scripts.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhang <emily@streamline.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: qa+perf@streamline.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo checklist — concurrency targets, k6 scripts, and allowlist window

Thanks Soojin — great summary. Quick responses: 

- k6 bundle: attaching our initial scenario bundle (streamline-k6-scenarios.tar.gz). It contains: sync-generation.js, auth.env, and a small README. Our sync profile uses a single prompt per request, median input length ~25 tokens.
- Streaming behavior: average 40 tokens/sec, median session length ~12s, 300 concurrent streams at peak, with some clients sending small follow-ups mid-stream.
- IP decision: we’d prefer Redwood to originate traffic for the main test so we can isolate client variability; please provide your IP ranges for allowlisting. We can run a second verification from our infra if needed.
- Test window: Thu 9/9 22:00–01:00 UTC works for us.

We don’t need any secrets other than the API key — please share the test credentials and any rate-limit policy you’ll apply to the account.

Attaching: streamline-k6-scenarios.tar.gz (scripts).

— Emily
Emily Zhang | Head of SRE, Streamline AI
emily@streamline.ai | +1 646-555-2102
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@streamline.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo checklist — concurrency targets, k6 scripts, and allowlist window

Emily — thanks for the bundle, looks good on first pass. Operational notes and what we’ll provision from Redwood: 

1) Test account + creds: I’ll create a temporary test account scoped to the demo model set (expires 2027-09-16). Credentials will be delivered via a one-time secret link.
2) IP allowlist: Redwood will originate traffic from the following ranges — please add to your inbound allowlist: 34.198.12.0/24, 54.210.33.0/24, 3.137.44.0/24.
3) Network NAT: tests originating from Redwood will be NATed (single IP per region) — we’ll include full CIDR blocks above.
4) Rate limiting / guardrails: we’ll enforce a soft concurrency cap per-model to protect production neighbors; for the test window we’ll set a tuned policy to allow your target throughput. If you see 429s, ping this thread immediately and we’ll lift the soft cap.
5) Observability: we’ll enable detailed token-level traces + request/response timing for the test window and share a Grafana link during the run.

Proposed runbook (we’ll publish to the Drive link and paste a short version here):
- 21:30 UTC: Redwood pre-warm (warm KV caches, populate model weights)
- 22:00 UTC: Start k6 sync ramp for 15 minutes up to 120 rps
- 22:20 UTC: Begin streaming probe, ramp to 300 concurrent streams over 10 minutes
- 22:50–23:50 UTC: Soak at target load; SLO checks + anomaly detection enabled
- 00:00–01:00 UTC: Controlled taper down, capture final traces

Attachments we’ll share before run: redwood-test-account-creds.txt (one-time), runbook link, temporary Grafana dashboard.

Notes/questions:
- Can you confirm if any of the streaming clients will occasionally send follow-ups that open new requests mid-stream? The scripts show small follow-ups; we want to ensure we model that in the token cadence.
- Also confirm whether TLS inspection/proxies are in front of your receivers — we need clear L4 pass-through for streaming.

I’ll create the test account now and post the secret link to this thread.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0188
From: Emily Zhang <emily@streamline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: qa+perf@streamline.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo checklist — concurrency targets, k6 scripts, and allowlist window

Thanks Marissa — confirm:
- We do have a small number (~10%) of streaming sessions that send a one-off follow-up mid-session; scripts include that.
- No TLS inspection / MITM proxies on our streaming endpoints — traffic will pass end-to-end.
- We have added the Redwood CIDRs to our ingress allowlist.

Please send the test API key link when ready. We’ll stand up our own observers and also watch the Grafana you provide. Looking forward to the run tomorrow night UTC.

— Emily
